Modern.tagline: Lighting designed for low northern light.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Filament names the heated wire at the core of an incandescent bulb — the original lighting trade word, in continuous use since Edison's 1879 carbon-filament demonstration. North anchors the brand to the Nordic design tradition of designing for long, dark winters (Henningsen, Wegner, Aalto). The pair reads as a modern lighting house with a specific lighting-design discipline.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern lighting has split into the design-led cohort (Hay, Muuto, Gubi) and the tech-led cohort (Dyson, Philips Hue). The opening is for a modern brand with the Nordic discipline of designing for low ambient light — the layered, glare-free systems pioneered by Poul Henningsen's PH series in 1925.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Hay (hay.com) holds the design-led modern peer. Muuto (muuto.com) plays the Nordic modern middle. Gubi (gubi.com) sits in the design-archive peer position. &Tradition (andtradition.com) is the Nordic heritage-modern reference. We sit alongside Muuto with a sharper low-light specialism.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern lighting brand designed for the eight months of the year when the sun barely shows up.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Maison is the French commercial-house convention used by heritage maisons (Maison Margiela, Maison Francis Kurkdjian). Lumière is French for 'light' — the foundational physical word for the category. The pair places the brand in the heritage French éclairagiste tradition (Baccarat, Lalique, Jansen) without imitating any specific maison.
Luxury.story: Maison Lumière is a French lighting house founded in 1922 in the Marais, Paris, and run by the founder's great-grandchildren. The catalog is nineteen fixtures — chandeliers, sconces, pendants, table lamps — each hand-finished in the original Paris atelier.
Luxury.industrySummary: Heritage lighting maisons are rare and remain among the most premium presentations available. There is space for a small French maison operating in the original family atelier register.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Baccarat (baccarat.com) is the institutional French luxury reference. Lalique (lalique.com) holds the heritage crystal peer slot. Charles Paris (charlesparis.com) sits in the small heritage maison middle. We belong with Charles Paris in the small French heritage maison category.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A French heritage lighting house with nineteen fixtures, hand-finished in the original Paris atelier since 1922.

Minimal.tagline: One lamp. Layered shade. Zero glare.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: PH references the multi-shade principle developed by Poul Henningsen and presented at the 1925 Paris Exposition — the layered-shade system that distributes light without glare. Zero strips the brand to a single fixture. The name reads as a typed catalog code, like a parts number.
Minimal.industrySummary: Lighting has accumulated apps, smart bulbs, seasonal collections, and decorative ranges. There's an opening for a brand that ships one fixture, one shade system, one colour.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most lighting brands fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some single-object Japanese lighting brands and certain architecture-school workshop lamps.
Minimal.positioningStatement: One lamp. Layered shade. Zero glare.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Lumen is the SI unit of luminous flux — the foundational technical word for the category. Industries signals a serious manufacturing operator. The pair reads as a real, established architectural lighting manufacturer already on the spec sheet of large firms.
Corporate.industrySummary: Architectural and commercial lighting is a B2B category dominated by large manufacturers (Acuity, Signify, Zumtobel). Buyers are architects, electrical contractors, and lighting designers specifying for offices, hotels, and institutional buildings. Brand and spec-grade reliability are the differentiators.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Acuity Brands (acuitybrands.com) is the institutional peer at scale. Signify (signify.com) holds the global manufacturer peer slot. Zumtobel (zumtobel.com) plays the European architectural peer. Erco (erco.com) sits in the design-led architectural middle. We sit closer to Erco with broader category coverage.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Architectural lighting manufacturing for serious specifiers.

Creative.tagline: A lighting brand for the hour the sun is gone.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Tungsten is the metal whose filament replaced Edison's carbon in 1904, and remains the trade word for warm incandescent light. Diary frames the brand as a storytelling object — a record of evenings. The pair reads as a warm, narrative lighting house with a strong character.
Creative.manifesto: Most lighting brands sell the fixture. We sell the hour. The hour after dinner. The reading lamp at 11pm. The bulb above the kitchen table while you finish the last of the wine. The brand is for that hour.
Creative.industrySummary: Lighting branding has been polished, architectural, and a little cold. There's room for one that's warm, narrative, character-driven, and serious about the way a room actually feels at night.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Tala (tala.co.uk) does the warm-glass middle. Original BTC (originalbtc.com) holds the considered British peer slot. Schoolhouse (schoolhouse.com) sits in the heritage-narrative peer position. We sit warmer and more narrative than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A lighting brand for the hour after dinner.
